articles.title: Proibição das bets: levantamento do MJ identifica, em 53 dias, 60 mil conteúdos ilegais sobre apostas | G1
articles.standfirst: Pesquisa considera sites, páginas, perfis de redes sociais, grupos e servidores em plataformas. Segundo o Ministério da Justiça, publicações alcançaram 204 milhões de usuários.
articles.summary: Pesquisa considera sites, páginas, perfis de redes sociais, grupos e servidores em plataformas. Segundo o Ministério da Justiça, publicações alcançaram 204 milhões de usuários.
articles.body:
O Ministério da Justiça enviou nesta terça-feira (17), ao Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ), uma nota técnica em que diz ter contabilizado mais de 60 mil conteúdos ligados à promoção de bets de 25 de setembro a 9 de novembro.

São publicações, páginas, perfis em redes sociais, grupos e servidores em plataformas.

O período corresponde aos primeiros 53 dias de vigência da medida provisória que proibiu a exploração dos jogos .

O documento foi elaborado pelo ministério para subsidiar as manifestações do governo durante a audiência pública que discutiu a proibição da atividade.

A audiência foi conduzida pelo ministro do STF Luiz Fux , relator de ações que contestam a medida do governo . Os documentos foram anexados pelo governo no processo relativos a essas ações.

Segundo o órgão, considerados os dados de audiência disponibilizados pelas plataformas, os registros identificados no período teriam alcançado aproximadamente 204,2 milhões de usuários .

O MJ afirmou, no entanto, que esse número representa a soma das audiências informadas para os diferentes ambientes digitais e não podem ser considerados usuários únicos, uma vez que pode haver sobreposição entre usuários de plataformas distintas.

“Os elementos consolidados nesta Nota Técnica demonstram a dimensão significativa da divulgação e da promoção de apostas irregulares no ambiente digital brasileiro, bem como a multiplicidade de canais utilizados para alcançar potenciais apostadores”, diz o documento.

“Nesse cenário, a Medida Provisória nº 1.394, de 2026, representa um avanço relevante na estrutura normativa de enfrentamento às apostas irregulares, ao estabelecer parâmetros mais claros para a identificação das atividades vedadas e ampliar os instrumentos disponíveis ao Poder Público para impedir sua exploração e divulgação”, conclui o ministério.

articles.title: Ajuste fiscal: Senado adia votação de destaques para quarta-feira | G1
articles.standfirst: Texto-base foi aprovado por 45 a 31. Restam cinco propostas de alteração no projeto, que podem alterar o alcance do corte gastos. Empresários reclamam que pagarão o custo.
articles.summary: Após aprovar o texto-base, senadores analisam mudanças que impactam créditos tributários de empresas e repasses da Lei Kandir a estados e municípios.
articles.body:
O Senado Federal adiou para quarta-feira (18) a votação das propostas de mudanças no projeto de lei complementar (PLP) do ajuste fiscal do governo do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) que podem reduzir o impacto nas contas públicas, os chamados destaques.

A expectativa era que os destaques fossem votados na sessão desta terça-feira (17), mas não houve acordo entre os senadores sobre quais propostas deveriam ser aprovadas ou rejeitadas.

Além disso, hoje os senadores ainda apresentaram outras sete novas emendas ao texto-base e que também deverão ser apreciados, mas apenas pelo relator da proposta, o senador Eduardo Braga (MDB-AM).

Na última quinta-feira (12), o plenário aprovou, por 45 votos a 31, o texto-base da proposta do governo para conter o crescimento das despesas públicas e aumentar a arrecadação na tentativa de estabilizar a dívida pública, preservando políticas sociais.

Para concluir a votação do projeto e enviar o texto aos deputados federais, os senadores precisam analisar cinco destaques:

excluir a autorização para o governo limitar o uso de créditos tributários por empresas;

reduzir de 2% para 0,6% o limite de crescimento das despesas e endurecer o controle de gastos;

excluir a redução temporária dos repasses da Lei Kandir a estados e municípios;

impedir a criação de um teto para as compensações previdenciárias, barrar créditos adicionais para investimentos e excluir o desconto dos subsídios ao diesel da meta de 2026;

destina o dinheiro que Poderes e órgãos autônomos economizarem ao cumprir o teto salarial para uso exclusivo para transferência de renda a famílias vulneráveis.

O último destaque foi apresentado nesta terça (17) pelo senador Alessandro Vieira (MDB-SE).

🔎 Destaque é um instrumento regimental utilizado pelos parlamentares para apreciar emenda ou subemenda que altere o texto-base de um projeto em discussão. Ele sempre acontece após a votação do texto principal.

Destaques mexem em créditos tributários, gastos e repasses

Um dos destaques que mais impacta o texto-base aprovado pelos senadores foi apresentado pelo líder do Republicanos, senador Alan Rick (Republicanos-AC), com uma emenda para retirar do texto a autorização que permite ao Executivo limitar o uso de créditos tributários por empresas para quitar impostos federais, caso a meta não seja atingida.

O dispositivo incluído no parecer do senador Eduardo Braga (MDB-AM) permite que o governo estabeleça restrições à compensação de tributos administrados pela Receita Federal.

Na prática, empresas que possuem créditos tributários poderiam ser obrigadas a desembolsar dinheiro para pagar parte dos impostos, mesmo tendo valores a receber do governo. Os percentuais de restrição seriam definidos posteriormente pelo Executivo.

Nos cálculos do governo, o dispositivo pode render um reforço na arrecadação de R$ 12,8 bilhões a R$ 18,3 bilhões em 2027.

O trecho que autoriza o Executivo a limitar a compensação de créditos tributários também motivou uma nota pública assinada por 119 entidades empresariais, entre elas a Confederação Nacional da Indústria (CNI), a Confederação da Agricultura e Pecuária do Brasil (CNA) e a Federação das Indústrias do Estado de São Paulo (Fiesp).

Para o grupo, o governo ganharia poder de restringir os créditos por conta própria, a cada contingenciamento preventivo, ainda que a meta fiscal esteja sendo cumprida. Os empresários pedem ao Congresso Nacional a exclusão total do dispositivo, com a manutenção das regras hoje em vigor.

Em uma proposta mais ampla, o PL apresentou um destaque para endurecer as regras de controle das despesas públicas e retirar medidas que permitem à União aumentar a arrecadação e adiar pagamentos.

Plenário do Senado Federal durante sessão deliberativa ordinária. Ordem do dia. — Foto: Carlos Moura/Agência Senado

A proposta, de iniciativa do líder da oposição no Senado, Rogério Marinho (PL-RN), assim como a do Republicanos, também prevê a retirada do artigo que permite ao governo restringir o uso de créditos tributários pelas empresas para quitar impostos federais, mas é ainda mais ampla.

A emenda prevê reduzir, a partir de 2027, de 2% para 0,6% o limite de crescimento real das despesas federais, ou seja, o aumento dos gastos acima da inflação, nos anos em que o governo adotasse as medidas de contenção previstas no projeto.

A emenda também obrigaria o Executivo a realizar cortes suficientes para alcançar, pelo menos, o centro da meta fiscal, mesmo quando o resultado projetado estivesse dentro da margem de tolerância permitida pelas regras atuais.

A proposta também amplia as possibilidades de contenção de gastos, permitindo que o governo possa reduzir ou cancelar despesas classificadas como obrigatórias, com exceção das obrigações constitucionais discriminadas na Lei de Diretrizes Orçamentárias (LDO).

Atualmente, essas despesas possuem maior proteção contra cortes, o que limita a capacidade do Executivo de ajustar o orçamento.

Além disso, a emenda também pretende impedir a redução temporária dos repasses da Lei Kandir a estados e municípios.

O texto de Braga limita essas transferências a R$ 1 bilhão por ano entre 2027 e 2030, ante os R$ 4 bilhões previstos atualmente, com pagamento posterior da diferença. O PL quer excluir a alteração e preservar o cronograma de pagamentos estabelecido pela legislação em vigor.

O PL, inclusive, tem um outro destaque para retirar exclusivamente do texto a redução temporária dos repasses da União a estados e municípios referentes à Lei Kandir.

🔎 A Lei Kandir estabelece que os produtos destinados à exportação não devem pagar o ICMS, tributo arrecadado pelos estados. O objetivo é tornar os produtos brasileiros competitivos no mercado internacional. A isenção provocou perda de arrecadação para os governos estaduais.

Para compensar, a União passou a transferir recursos aos estados e municípios. Em 2020, uma nova lei complementar estabeleceu um acordo para o pagamento dessas compensações, com repasses anuais de R$ 4 bilhões até 2030 e valores menores nos anos seguintes, até 2037.

É justamente esse pagamento que o projeto relatado por Eduardo Braga pretende alterar, reduzindo temporariamente os repasses previstos entre 2027 e 2030 e determinando que a diferença seja paga posteriormente.

Após a aprovação do texto-base, o Comitê Nacional de Secretários de Fazenda, Finanças, Receita ou Tributação dos Estados e do Distrito Federal (Comsefaz) publicou uma nota manifestando preocupação com a redução nos repasses da Lei Kandir.

Segundo o Comsefaz, a medida retira do caixa de estados e municípios R$ 3 bilhões em 2027. Até 2030, segundo a nota, o montante será R$ 12 bilhões: aproximadamente R$ 9 bilhões dos governos estaduais e R$ 3 bilhões das prefeituras.

“Embora preserve o montante nominal de R$ 58 bilhões, o adiamento de parte dos repasses reduz o valor econômico da obrigação assumida pela União e rompe o equilíbrio do acordo”, diz a nota do Comsefaz.

A oposição propõe ainda retirar as restrições à compensação previdenciária entre regimes de aposentadoria, impedir a abertura de créditos adicionais para investimentos estruturantes prevista no projeto e excluir a autorização para descontar parte dos subsídios ao diesel do cálculo da meta fiscal de 2026.

A emenda também altera as regras de utilização de recursos de fundos públicos e determina que a economia obtida com o combate aos supersalários seja integralmente descontada do limite de despesas.

Em outro destaque do PL, a proposta é impedir a criação de um limite anual para os pagamentos de compensações previdenciárias da União a estados e municípios, incluído no texto de Braga.

A compensação previdenciária é um mecanismo utilizado para acertar as contas entre o INSS e os regimes de aposentadoria dos servidores públicos.

Quando um trabalhador contribui para o INSS e depois se aposenta por um regime estadual ou municipal, por exemplo, a União deve compensar financeiramente o governo responsável pelo pagamento da aposentadoria, conforme o período de contribuição aproveitado.

O projeto estabelece um teto inicial de R$ 3 bilhões por ano para essas compensações entre 2027 e 2030, com correção anual vinculada ao crescimento do limite de despesas do arcabouço fiscal.

Segundo estimativa da Confederação Nacional de Municípios (CNM), a medida pode reduzir os repasses previdenciários em aproximadamente R$ 5 bilhões por ano, acumulando mais de R$ 20 bilhões até 2030.

Diferentemente da redução das compensações da Lei Kandir, o texto não estabelece um cronograma para o pagamento posterior dos valores que ultrapassarem o limite. Se o destaque do PL for aprovado, o teto será retirado do projeto e permanecerão as regras atuais de compensação previdenciária.

Em manifestações separadas, divulgadas na quinta-feira (12) quando o texto-base foi votado, CNI, Fiesp e a Federação das Indústrias do Estado de Minas Gerais (Fiemg) sustentaram que os grandes empresários arcarão com a maior parte do custo do ajuste.

A CNI afirmou que o Congresso já derrubou tentativas semelhantes de restringir compensações.

Entre os municípios, a Confederação Nacional de Municípios (CNM) foi além das críticas pontuais e solicitou ao Congresso que rejeite o projeto por inteiro.

Pelas contas da entidade, as prefeituras deixarão de receber mais de R$ 32 bilhões até 2030, somados R$ 20 bilhões das compensações previdenciárias e R$ 12 bilhões da Lei Kandir.

articles.title: Na expectativa de votar ajuste fiscal na Câmara, governo retira urgência de projeto sobre criminalização de bets | G1
articles.standfirst: Proposta que tipifica os crimes de exploração e divulgação de apostas impediria qualquer votação no plenário nesta semana; bets continuam proibidas no país.
articles.summary: Proposta que tipifica os crimes de exploração e divulgação de apostas impediria qualquer votação no plenário nesta semana; bets continuam proibidas no país.
articles.body:
Acesso bloqueado Brasil Sem Bets bets site celular — Foto: Isabela Ortiz/g1

O governo Lula (PT) retirou nesta terça-feira (17) a urgência do projeto que tipifica os crimes de exploração e divulgação de bets . O texto trancaria, ou seja, impediria outras votações no plenário da Câmara nesta semana, incluindo a proposta de ajuste fiscal da administração petista.

A retirada da urgência foi oficializada no Diário Oficial da União desta terça (17). O governo havia imposto o regime no fim de setembro.

🔎 Pela Constituição, uma proposta enviada pelo Poder Executivo pode tramitar em urgência a pedido do presidente da República. No caso, o texto precisaria ser votado dentro de 45 dias na Câmara. Como o prazo venceu na última quinta-feira (12), nenhum projeto pode ser votado até que o texto que cria os crimes relacionados às bets seja votado ou o governo retirasse a urgência.

🔎 A proposta do governo tem como objetivo conter o crescimento das despesas e aumentar a arrecadação na tentativa de estabilizar a dívida pública, sem abrir mão de políticas sociais.

O ajuste fiscal ainda está em votação no Senado, que precisa terminar de votar partes específicas do texto nos quais não há acordo, os chamados destaques . Os senadores devem finalizar a votação e enviar o texto direto para o plenário da Câmara.

“A ideia é que hoje, daqui para de noite, a gente possa garantir a vitória. Com a conclusão do Senado, começa imediatamente a votação da Câmara. Foi um compromisso do presidente Hugo Motta esperar chegar do Senado e votar imediatamente ainda hoje”, afirmou nesta terça o ministro das Relações Institucionais, José Guimarães.

A pressa se dá porque o governo quer que as novas regras constem na lei orçamentária de 2027 – que deve ser votada no Congresso nas próximas semanas.

Também conta para a tentativa de encerrar tudo nesta terça-feira (17) a provável ausência do presidente da Câmara, Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB), na quarta-feira (18) para participar de um evento internacional.

Para agilizar a aprovação, o ministro do Planejamento e Orçamento, Bruno Moretti, deve fazer uma reunião com os deputados do PT para retirar as últimas dúvidas sobre o texto. As críticas de partes de integrantes às medidas é de que novas restrições aos gastos podem comprometer serviços públicos e investimentos.

O ministro do Planejamento e Orçamento, Bruno Moretti. — Foto: Fábio Rodrigues Pozzebom/Agência Brasil

Líderes do governo e Moretti, no entanto, têm reforçado que é preciso criar espaço no Orçamento exatamente para manter políticas sociais e promessas feitas pelo presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) em sua campanha vitoriosa pela reeleição.

O projeto enviado pelo governo Lula e que agora deve ser votado somente em outro momento pela Câmara institui os seguintes crimes e penas:

Exploração de aposta de quota fixa – de 4 a 6 anos de prisão e multa;

Divulgação de aposta de quota fixa – de 2 a 4 anos de prisão e multa;

Uso de dados pessoais para captar apostadores - de 2 a 4 anos de prisão e multa;

Facilitar a exploração financeira de bets - de 2 a 4 anos de prisão e multa; e

Fornecer aplicativos para exploração de bets - de 2 a 4 anos de prisão e multa.

Mesmo sem a tipificação dos crimes, a proibição para a exploração de bets no Brasil continuam valendo . O veto foi feito pelo presidente Lula por meio de uma Medida Provisória, que continua válida.

articles.title: Ajuste fiscal: governo busca aprovação na Câmara e no Senado hoje | G1
articles.standfirst: Texto ainda está em análise no Senado, onde possíveis alterações devem ser votadas nesta terça. Motta disse que deputados estão preocupados com a alta do dólar e os juros altos.
articles.summary: O ajuste fiscal passa por votação decisiva no Congresso nesta terça para conter o dólar e os juros, sob articulação de Hugo Motta e pressão da base aliada.
articles.body:
O ministro das Relações Institucionais, José Guimarães, afirmou nesta terça-feira (17) que o governo tem um acordo com o presidente da Câmara dos Deputados , Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB), para pautar e votar o projeto de ajuste fiscal ainda nesta terça.

Em entrevista, Motta disse que a Casa está disposta a votar o texto ainda nesta terça caso a proposta seja encaminhada pelo Senado . Ele afirmou que o tema será relatado pelo deputado Mauro Benevides Filho (União-CE).

"Nós estamos muito preocupados com essa alta do dólar, a perspectiva de uma alta taxa de juros e defendemos que o governo possa, além desse ajuste, poder também construir outras saídas que possam garantir a estabilidade econômica", declarou .

O texto-base foi aprovado no Senado na semana passada, por 45 votos a 31. Mas ainda falta a votação de quatro destaques (propostas de mudanças no texto) previstos para serem analisados nesta tarde, antes de o projeto seguir para a Câmara dos Deputados.

🔎 A proposta do governo tem como objetivo conter o crescimento das despesas e aumentar a arrecadação na tentativa de estabilizar a dívida pública, sem abrir mão de políticas sociais.

"Aqui no Congresso, nós continuamos compromissados com essa agenda, tanto é que anuncio aqui a nossa disposição de ainda hoje [terça] apreciarmos essa matéria e, com isso, podemos dar uma demonstração da parceria entre o Executivo e Legislativo, na busca de um ambiente e normalidade econômica para o nosso país", disse ainda o presidente da Câmara.

Já o presidente do Senado, Davi Alcolumbre (União-AP), afirmou que ainda estão buscando acordo para votar os destaques e que se a tramitação for concluída no Senado nesta terça, segue imediatamente para a Câmara.

Líder do governo na Câmara, deputado José Guimarães (PT-CE) — Foto: GloboNews

O ministro José Guimarães chamou o dia de “super terça”, reforçando que o governo está empenhado em aprovar a pauta nas duas Casas o quanto antes.

“A ideia é que hoje, daqui para de noite, a gente possa garantir a vitória. Com a conclusão do Senado, começa imediatamente a votação da Câmara. Foi um compromisso do presidente Hugo Motta esperar chegar do Senado e votar imediatamente ainda hoje”, afirmou Guimarães.

Ele deu a declaração à imprensa ao lado da líder do governo no Senado, Teresa Leitão (PT-PE), após reunião de lideranças do partido no Palácio do Planalto.

Os quatro destaques que serão analisados pelos senadores tratam de:

excluir a autorização para o governo limitar o uso de créditos tributários por empresas;

reduzir de 2% para 0,6% o limite de crescimento das despesas e endurecer o controle de gastos;

excluir a redução temporária dos repasses da Lei Kandir a estados e municípios;

impedir a criação de um teto para as compensações previdenciárias, barrar créditos adicionais para investimentos e excluir o desconto dos subsídios ao diesel da meta de 2026.

O ministro Guimarães também comentou as divergências entre os políticos do PT sobre o texto do ajuste fiscal. Afirmou que o debate é legítimo e que faz parte da natureza do partido.

O projeto de ajuste fiscal defendido pelo governo do presidente Lula (PT) abriu uma disputa dentro da esquerda sobre os rumos da política econômica no próximo mandato.

A divergência envolve integrantes do próprio PT, parlamentares de partidos aliados e movimentos sociais que apoiaram a reeleição do presidente.

Enquanto a equipe econômica defende que as medidas são necessárias para equilibrar as contas e preservar as políticas sociais, críticos afirmam que novas restrições aos gastos podem comprometer serviços públicos e investimentos.

Também questionam a falta de diálogo com a base e a velocidade da tramitação no Congresso.

“É importante dizer pra vocês que nós estamos unificados e que vamos trabalhar para unificar as bancadas. Para nós é absolutamente legítimo o debate interno que a esquerda está fazendo. Só quem não conhece o PT é que não entende esses problemas que surgem, que a gente debate, que a gente articula e que a gente vota”, disse Guimarães.

O chefe da Secretaria de Relações Institucionais destacou ainda que “não tem crise” mas sim “divergências, como acontece sempre na esquerda”.

Teresa Leitão (PT-PE), líder do governo no Senado, destacou a necessidade do ajuste fiscal e afirmou que ele é essencial para a discussão do Orçamento de 2027.

“[O texto] tem o conteúdo necessário porque dialoga com a aprovação do orçamento, uma peça robusta e estruturante que vai dizer, em cada área do governo, onde é que o dinheiro vai ficar".

Segundo a senadora, se o governo não tiver “esse colchão, o orçamento vai virar uma peça decorativa que a gente não quer”.

articles.title: Brasil Soberano: Senado aprova R$ 13,5 bi para exportadores | G1
articles.standfirst: Proposta ficou conhecida como “Brasil Soberano”. Conjunto de medidas inclui linhas de crédito, garantias para exportadores, benefícios tributários e ações para ampliar a abertura de novos mercados.
articles.summary: Com R$ 13,5 bilhões, o Brasil Soberano apoiará exportadores afetados por tarifas dos EUA e pela guerra no Oriente Médio após aprovação do Senado Federal.
articles.body:
O Senado Federal aprovou nesta terça-feira (17) a medida provisória que criou o programa Brasil Soberano 3 , para minimizar os efeitos das tarifas impostas pelos Estados Unidos sobre produtos brasileiros e também aquelas impactadas pela guerra no Oriente Médio.

Com a aprovação, a proposta segue para sanção presidencial.

🔎 O plano Brasil Soberano é um conjunto de medidas criadas pelo governo federal para apoiar a indústria brasileira, liberando linhas de crédito, garantias para exportadores, benefícios tributários e ações para ampliar a abertura de novos mercados.

➡️ A tarifa de 25% sobre produtos brasileiros, que começou a valer em julho, é resultado de uma investigação comercial do Escritório de Comércio dos EUA (USTR, na sigla em inglês), órgão responsável por formular a política comercial norte-americana.

➡️ A guerra no Oriente Médio prejudicou o transporte marítimo no Golfo Pérsico. Uma das principais rotas do comércio de petróleo passava pelo Estreito de Ormuz, que foi fechado em meio aos conflitos entre Irã, EUA e Israel.

Do montante total, R$ 5 bilhões será destinado especificamente ao apoio de exportadores e de cadeias de fornecimento afetados pelo aumento das alíquotas de tarifas aplicadas pelo governo norte-americano.

Outros R$ 3,5 bilhões serão alocados para companhias e fornecedores que comercializam com países do Golfo Pérsico , com o objetivo de amortecer os reflexos econômicos decorrentes do conflito no Oriente Médio.

R$ 2 bilhões vão para projetos industriais e tecnológicos nas etapas de lavra associadas a beneficiamento, refino ou transformação de minerais;

R$ 2 bilhões serão direcionados à produção e fabricação de fertilizantes ou de intermediários para o setor;

R$ 1 bilhão vai para setores industriais de relevância para a balança comercial brasileira.

Poderão ter acesso às linhas de crédito do Brasil Soberano:

empresas, cooperativas e associações exportadoras de bens industriais, bem como seus respectivos fornecedores

produtores e exportadores de produtos da agricultura, pecuária e pesca

empresas e fornecedores ligados à exportação de recursos minerais

Os beneficiários poderão utilizar os recursos para aquisição de máquinas, reforço do capital de giro, inovação tecnológica, entre outras finalidades.

A fiscalização e o acompanhamento das operações ficarão a cargo do Banco Nacional de Desenvolvimento Econômico e Social (BNDES).

O banco deverá enviar relatórios mensais ao Conselho Interministerial do Plano Brasil Soberano, detalhando o volume de propostas aprovadas, contratos firmados e valores efetivamente desembolsados.

China dribla tarifaço de Trump e tem superávit comercial de US$ 1 trilhão pela primeira vez na história — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

O Brasil Soberano é uma medida criada pelo governo federal via BNDES para apoiar empresas brasileiras em momentos de instabilidade no cenário internacional. O programa oferece linhas de crédito para empresas exportadoras.

O plano foi criado no ano passado para oferecer apoio financeiro aos exportadores que foram afetados no primeiro tarifaço.

Nesta segunda etapa do plano, o crédito será destinado a empresas exportadoras e seus fornecedores que sofrem os impactos do segundo "tarifaço" imposto pelos Estados Unidos aos produtos brasileiros. A medida também alcança empresas afetadas pela instabilidade no Golfo Pérsico e setores industriais considerados importantes para as exportações do país.

articles.title: Marco Buzzi: STJ determina desocupação de apartamento funcional | G1
articles.standfirst: Ministro do STJ foi punido pela Corte após denúncias de assédio sexual. Na semana passada, o STF decidiu manter o afastamento de Buzzi, mas manteve salário.
articles.summary: O presidente do STJ, Luis Felipe Salomão, determinou que o ministro afastado Marco Buzzi desocupe o apartamento funcional após punição por assédio sexual.
articles.body:
O presidente do Superior Tribunal de Justiça (STJ), ministro Luis Felipe Salomão , determinou que o ministro afastado Marco Buzzi desocupe o apartamento funcional situado na Asa Sul, em Brasília, no prazo de 90 dias .

Além da devolução do imóvel, a decisão desta terça-feira (17) impõe a restituição de equipamentos, e bens públicos sob a responsabilidade do magistrado, bem como a adequação de credenciais e acessos institucionais.

A nova determinação é um desdobramento da decisão do STJ de agosto em agosto, quando o Plenário da Corte decidiu punir Marco Buzzi e recomendou a perda do cargo após denúncias de assédio sexual .

Na ocasião, a Corte entendeu que a gravidade das condutas atribuídas ao magistrado justificava a sanção disciplinar máxima que pode ser aplicada no âmbito administrativo.

Na semana passada, o Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ) manteve o afastamento de Buzzi do STJ , preservando o pagamento de seus vencimentos enquanto a ação que discute a perda definitiva do cargo não é julgada em definitivo pela Suprema Corte.

Na decisão desta terça, o presidente do STJ afirmou que o uso de imóveis funcionais e o pagamento de auxílio-moradia não podem ser dissociados do efetivo exercício da atividade de ministro.

Conforme o despacho, vantagens de gabinete deixam de existir quando o agente público é afastado das funções por sanção disciplinar.

Ministro Marco Buzzi do STJ — Foto: Gustavo Lima/STJ

Marco Buzzi está afastado do cargo desde 10 de fevereiro, quando foi aberto o processo disciplinar contra ele. O magistrado é alvo de duas denúncias no STJ, além de um inquérito no STF.

A Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR) aponta que as vítimas apresentaram relatos firmes, coerentes e convergentes com as provas do processo.

Duas denúncias contra o magistrado foram analisadas:

uma jovem de 18 anos afirma ter sido vítima de importunação sexual, durante um banho de mar, em janeiro de 2026, quando passava férias com a família na casa de Buzzi em Balneário Camboriú (SC); e

uma ex-funcionária de gabinete relatou episódios reiterados de assédio sexual e importunação cometidos enquanto trabalhava na equipe do magistrado no STJ.

A PGR entendeu que no caso da jovem de 18 anos há elementos que demonstram que Buzzi teria "violado o dever de manter conduta irrepreensível na vida particular [...] bem como deixado de observar as regras da integridade, da dignidade, da honra e do decoro".

No caso da ex-funcionária, a procuradoria diz que ficou comprovada violação dos "deveres de urbanidade e de manter conduta irrepreensível na vida particular [...] bem como a inobservância das regras da integridade, da cortesia, da dignidade, da honra e do decoro".

articles.title: GOP Rep. James Comer announces bid for Kentucky governor
articles.summary: Rep. James Comer, R-Ky., announced Monday night that he is running for governor of Kentucky in an attempt to flip the governor’s mansion from blue to red in...
articles.body:
Rep. James Comer, R-Ky., announced Monday night that he is running for governor of Kentucky in an attempt to flip the governor's mansion from blue to red in 2027.

The Republican congressman's announcement comes on the heels this month's blue tsunami that swept Democrats into control of both chambers of Congress.

Democratic Gov. Andy Beshear, who is term limited, has led Kentucky since 2019, though voters backed Republicans for statewide positions in the midterm elections.

Comer announced his candidacy in a tele-town hall, where he took questions from callers. While answering one of the questions, the congressman sought to create some distance from President Donald Trump.

"I think that some of the things the president has tried to do on the national level had good intentions, but there are always unintended consequences," said Comer, who like many House Republicans aligned himself with Trump over the years.

Comer was first elected to Congress in 2016. He currently serves as chair of the House Oversight Committee, which oversaw Congress' probe into Jeffrey Epstein .

Kentucky is one of the few states to have off-year elections for governor — the others are Louisiana and Mississippi. The 2027 election could be an early test of how durable the blue wave will prove one year out from the midterm elections — and a year before the 2028 presidential election.

Trump won Kentucky by more than 30 percentage points in 2024, and Comer won re-election this year by an even wider margin, defeating his Democratic opponent by more than 35 points.

Comer is the biggest name to jump into the race on the GOP side. Three other Republicans have declared their intentions to run, including former reality TV contestant Charles "Bruiser" Martin and Rick Hardin, a state attorney.

On the Democratic side, Lt. Gov. Jacqueline Coleman and former Beshear senior adviser Rocky Adkins have said they are running.

Kentucky will hold its primaries on May 18.

Sam Newton, a spokesperson for the Democratic Governors Association, criticized Comer in a statement while expressing confidence the governorship will stay in Democratic hands after next year's election.

"The DGA just beat Republican members of Congress who ran for governor in states like Arizona, Michigan, and Wisconsin and we're excited to add Kentucky to that list," Newton said.

Democrats this month won the majority of governorships for the first time in 16 years.

Beshear currently serves as chair of the DGA.

articles.title: Trump and Immigration Reform: Will Democrats make him an offer he can't refuse?
articles.summary: Trump signals he's open to negotiating regularization for nonviolent immigrants but warns Democrats that impeachment efforts could kill any deal.
articles.body: It is test time again for Democrats. They know how to campaign against President Donald Trump when he is not on the ballot for the presidency. But does the Democratic Party actually want to accomplish something for immigrants who are in the country illegally? Many of their candidates swept in by the blue tsunami of two weeks ago, campaigned on helping the millions of immigrants who entered the country illegally during President Joe Biden’s term. But will they deliver that group … anything? Because if the Democrats actually want to do that, Trump is ready to begin negotiations. TRUMP OPENS DOOR TO IMMIGRATION DEAL, BUT REPUBLICANS HAVE ONE CONDITION If the Democrats actually wanted to accomplish something for immigrants who are in the United States without the legal right to be here, the new speaker of the House and the new majority leader in the Senate could present Trump many different and acceptable pieces of legislation addressing some or all of those immigrants. If the proposals are reasonable, a genuine negotiation would follow between the president and the Democratic majorities over what they both wanted, and each could get most of what they want done. If Democrats want a blanket amnesty, that won’t work. If they demand a "path to citizenship and voting," that would be a bridge too far. But if they seek "regularization" of people who are nonviolent and willing to work? TRUMP TELLS DHS CHIEF TO WORK WITH DEMOCRATS ON IMMIGRATION REFORM, BUT NO AMNESTY On Thursday, I asked Trump: "If Hakeem Jeffries and Chuck Schumer come up, and they want the DREAMers, or they want regularization for people who aren’t violent in the country, what are you going to want?" "[G]reat things can be done between the Democrats and the Republicans on healthcare," Trump said. "And if I can do that with the Democrats, I’d love to do that." DEMOCRATS PLOT MASSIVE SPENDING SPREE AFTER MIDTERM ROUT — AND TRUMP COULD HELP THEM PULL IT OFF That exchange followed the president laying out a "condition precedent" of sorts (the legal term for an event or requirement that must occur or be satisfied before a contractual obligation becomes enforceable, or a party is required to perform its side of any deal). "Maybe I wouldn’t want to, because it’s in such bad, you know, when I negotiate, I negotiate in good faith. If they’re doing that, it’s in bad faith." So, quite simply, every potential subject of legislation, including "regularization" of millions of illegal immigrants, is on the table when the new Congress arrives, but the table itself vanishes if the Democrats want to investigate rather than legislate. If Democrats want a blanket amnesty, that won’t work. If they demand a "path to citizenship and voting," that would be a bridge too far. To get to a deal, the "get Trump" Democrats would have to set aside their deep desire to grandstand so that they could accomplish some sort of security for the 10 to 20 million immigrants in the United States who are in danger of deportation if they cross the path of ICE. AT LEAST 9 NEW DEM MEMBERS WILL CARRY AL GREEN'S MANTLE AND TRY TO IMPEACH PRESIDENT TRUMP Which is why the immigrant communities have their hopes up. The goal of the conditional right to remain — a felony conviction would of course end a conditional visa — is within reach. But such hopes were dashed by President Barack Obama when he had his large majorities in both the House and the Senate in January 2009, and again by Biden in January 2021 when he was supported by majorities in both houses of Congress. Both men abandoned this constituency. JEFFRIES PROMISES ‘REMEDIAL ASSISTANCE’ TO ANYONE IMPACTED BY TRUMP IMMIGRATION ENFORCEMENT Because being a Democratic leader means never having to say you are sorry to the people who trusted you. Which is why the exile the GOP is about to enter in Congress isn’t remotely permanent or even likely to be long. articles.title: Trump's $50B air traffic control overhaul faces GOP pushback after nationwide ground stop
articles.summary: Senate Republicans want receipts on the $12.5 billion already sent for air traffic control as the Trump administration seeks $50 billion more.
articles.body: The Trump administration is pressing Congress for tens of billions in emergency funding to upgrade the nation’s air traffic control systems, but even Senate Republicans are reluctant to pay the bill. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and President Donald Trump called on lawmakers to shell out $50 billion in funding after a ground stop on Friday caused thousands of flight cancellations and blamed Congress for not doling out money previously to upgrade aging air traffic control communications infrastructure. But Congress did send $12.5 billion to the Department of Transportation as part of the "big, beautiful bill" last year meant to upgrade the archaic systems, and Republicans want receipts on what happened to the money. FAA SAYS AIR TRAVEL SHOULD BE BACK TO NORMAL SUNDAY AFTER NATIONWIDE GROUND STOP "Only about four [billion] has been spent," Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., said. "There was about eight billion of that still sitting around." Duffy is slated to meet with Senate Republicans behind closed doors on Tuesday where lawmakers expect a full breakdown of what happened and where the money has gone and why, suddenly, the administration is seeking an additional $20 billion. "I haven't seen how they're gonna use it. I mean, in my business, you know, I spent a lot of money, and I built companies," Sen. Rick Scott, R-Fla., told Fox News Digital. "And I understood what I was going to spend it on before I ever did anything. I'd have a budget and what the timeline is, who's gonna do it, all that stuff." FORMER TOP FAA OFFICIAL WARNS OF 48-HOUR RECOVERY AFTER AGING TECH 'OVERWHELMED' AHEAD OF GROUND STOP Data from the Department of Transportation (DOT) obtained by Fox News Digital showed that roughly $3.7 billion had been spent on a variety of projects, while the remainder is tied to contracts, unspent or planned for near-term upgrades, like facility consolidation. Thune declined to say whether he had confidence in Duffy’s handling of the situation and noted that the administration had already made a separate ask for $30 billion, a chunk of which was meant to continue upgrades to air traffic control. "I mean, there's some explanations that have to be given as to why that number is where it is," Thune said. "But I think we have attempted to do everything we can to ensure that the concerns they have about modernization are being met." Duffy’s explanation of the ground stop was attributed to replacing copper wiring in communications equipment with fiber-optic cable. About $4.8 billion of the initial funding pot was for copper wire replacement, of which about $2.3 billion has been spent, which translates to roughly 70% completion of the telecommunications replacement program, according to the DOT. 4 CRITICAL TRAVEL ISSUES FOR THOSE DELAYED AND DISRUPTED BY FAA NATIONWIDE GROUND STOP A DOT spokesperson told Fox News Digital that the "Department has made clear for the last two years — separate funding is needed" for other work because DOT "does not have the legal flexibility to move funds from one workstream to another." Still, lawmakers have questions. "He needs to talk to me like I'm a reasonably intelligent 10th grader," Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., said. "The American people are not experts on telecommunications … nor am I." Kennedy, who is a member of the Transportation, Housing and Urban Development Appropriations Subcommittee, which controls the DOT's purse strings, said he was more than "willing to appropriate money to fix this," but needed to understand the problem first. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "I mean, we had an outage today, some problems with a number of our banks," Kennedy said. "There have been some problems in Europe with the Internet controlling temperatures of grocery stores. I mean, this is happening a lot. I'm not saying there's a connection, but if there is, they need to tell us." Sen. James Lankford, R-Okla., told Fox News Digital that the initial $12.5 billion was "a starting point — it wasn’t everything." "We've seen nothing yet of what's the rest of the request," Lankford said. "So that does seem like, ‘Hey, grab a number out of the air. It needs to be big.’" Lankford added that Duffy needed to give a "postmortem" on what happened, and that whatever the administration is asking for in upgrades needs to be "shovel-ready." "This is a zero fail operation," he said. "He's keenly aware of that."

articles.title: Hundreds protest against ex-border patrol chief Greg Bovino at Rutgers University talk
articles.summary: New Jersey university’s Republicans club invited Bovino, who oversaw Trump’s ICE surges, to speak on campus
articles.body:
Hundreds protested outside a Rutgers University campus building on Monday night, jeering the former border patrol commander Greg Bovino, who was inside addressing a crowd of about 25 people.

The university's Republicans club had invited Bovino to speak, calling him the "Great Commander" and the "GOAT" in social posts promoting the event at the New Brunswick, New Jersey, campus. During the two-hour talk, the room never quite filled up, occupied mostly by journalists, club members and other students criticizing the former border patrol chief.

"Show of hands, can we remove 100 million illegal aliens by 2028? Do you think we can?" Bovino asked the crowd. Two or three hands went into the air. "Well, I'm telling you what, my hand's raised! American exceptionalism! We can do it before then!"

Bovino was the face of the Trump administration's immigration crackdown, overseeing massive Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) surges in Chicago, Minneapolis and other US cities. Scrutiny and public outrage over agents' brutal handling of immigrant arrests, pulling children off the streets and taking people from cars, only intensified after agents killed the Minneapolis residents Alex Pretti and Renee Good in January. Bovino, who argued Pretti was a "suspect" rather than a victim, was taken out of the field by the end of the month and retired in March, reportedly while under internal investigation .

A few minutes into his talk on Monday, about a dozen protesters drowned out his remarks. "What's so crazy is that you all allowed a Nazi to be here," one protester shouted over him, standing from her seat.

"Your fascist death cult is failing!" yelled another. Several police officers gathered in front of a grinning Bovino on stage, who seemed to be relishing the attention.

Helping lead the disruption was immigration advocate Gabriela Soto, whose husband, Martín, helped lead hunger strikes over conditions and deaths at the Delaney Hall immigration detention facility in New Jersey earlier this year. When Martín was transferred to another facility in May , intense protests ensued for weeks .

Gabriela was pregnant when Martín was taken into ICE custody; while he was held in solitary confinement, she miscarried.

"You're taking children!" she screamed, standing on a chair at the Rutgers event. "It's not OK!"

Bovino eventually left the stage for a few minutes, while police ordered protesters to either stop the disruption or disperse; they largely complied. He then returned to give his talk, in which he repeatedly mentioned a small Michigan city that banned LGBTQ+ pride flags in 2023, made a seemingly homophobic pun out of Pete Buttigieg's last name and ridiculed New Jersey's governor, Mikie Sherrill, who earlier on Monday issued a statement condemning the event without ordering its cancellation.

Even among the smaller crowd, multiple people expressed their disagreement with Bovino during a question-and-answer session. When retired teacher Alan Cummings asked about his goal of 100m deportations, even though the estimated number of undocumented immigrants in the US is a fraction of that, he argued Cummings wasn't proud to be American.

After Rutgers's College Republicans announced the event last month, it was immediately met with backlash. The ICE Out of New Jersey coalition , comprising several advocacy organizations, and student organizers called on the university to cancel it. The students' petition garnered more than 2,000 signatures.

Dory Devlin, assistant vice-president of news and media relations at Rutgers, said the university was committed to freedom of expression, but that "providing space for a student-organized event does not constitute university endorsement of the speaker or the views expressed".

"We are all about free speech," said Brea Yumiguano, a Rutgers senior and student organizer with Climate Revolution Action Network. "The issue comes when it's Greg Bovino, someone who has been violent in the past, who has eroded our constitutional rights, who's pepper-sprayed protesters in Minneapolis – that's not what we want in New Brunswick."

Yumiguano and other students at the protest talked about the lack of safety facing immigrant students, students with immigrant family members and international students who fear being targeted by ICE. Earlier that Monday, it was reported that US international student enrollment had dropped for the second consecutive year amid the Trump administration's ICE campaign.

A Rutgers sophomore named Ninnie broke down in tears while telling the crowd she did not feel safe bringing her family to campus, describing reports of ICE agents targeting local public transportation. "There are plenty of us students here who are people of color who are afraid to have our family members come visit us at Rutgers," she told the crowd.

After more than an hour of chanting to drums and bagpipes, most of the protesters left. Eventually, those who remained at Bovino's talk trickled out through the security perimeter established by police. A "prosecute Bovino" sign was left by the exit door.

"This is an example of what New Jersey is about: New Jersey is an immigrants' rights state. We welcome immigrants," said Jorge Torres of the National Day Laborer Organizing Network, a member of the ICE Out coalition. Torres was among those who interrupted Bovino's speech. "We don't want no neo-Nazis in our state."

images.caption: Protesters disrupt former border patrol commander Greg Bovino's appearance at the Rutgers University campus in New Brunswick, New Jersey, on Monday. Photograph: Olga Fedorova/EPA

articles.title: Let's be honest, no politician is coming to save you, so save yourself first
articles.summary: A Chicago pastor who spent 94 days on a motel roof after gang violence killed 16-year-old Carlton Archer says elections won't pay your rent.
articles.body: Two weeks ago, on Nov. 3, many of us Americans voted. We watched the election returns come in on cable and broadcast news that night. We were flooded with takes on the results from so-called media experts. And now our newly elected officials are waiting in the wings to take office in the new year. But for most of us, on the first of the month, the rent will still be due. I say this because our elected officials are not our saviors. I didn’t vote for either of Chicago’s last two mayors. Neither one of them did much for our community. Nor will the newly elected, despite all of their promises. Down here on the South Side of Chicago, I have mothers who let their mailboxes overflow because they’re afraid of seeing the bills they can’t pay. There are fathers looking for work. Too many of our young people have watched their friends get buried or locked up. And the rent, the light bill, the groceries and the car note do not care who won the election. I believe we give far too much credit to politicians. The best of our society often do not run for office, and those representing us are not the best of us. We cannot afford false idols any longer. In my community work, I tell people to forget about anyone coming to save their butt. The first one who is going to save you is you. You have to save yourself before anyone can help you. PASTOR COREY BROOKS: EL-SAYED'S PITCH TO BLACK VOTERS IS THE SAME OLD LIBERAL CONDESCENSION I learned that the hard way. I didn’t grow up here. I was born in Kenton, Tennessee, and raised in Muncie, Indiana. I thought I wanted to be a lawyer until I heard God calling me. I became a pastor, and I eventually came to Chicago, where I started my New Beginnings Church in 2000. I started this church for young people who had never been connected to a church. In those early years, I was told I had to be part of the political machine to get things done. I remember people trying to get me on the Jesse Jackson bandwagon, and I met with a lot of those people. However, I felt a profound disconnect between that world of politics, racial politics, and the Christian work I was doing on the ground with my congregation. The violence was out of control. The drug use was ungodly. The number of single-parent households was staggering. My issue with this Chicago political machine was that the solution was always political. These politicians held themselves out as the solutions. Their policies were the solutions. Yet things got worse. DIVINE PURPOSE HELPED BRING CHICAGO’S MOST-DANGEROUS BLOCK BACK TO LIFE Then, in 2011, I received the terrible news that Carlton Archer, a 16-year-old boy, had been shot. He was a member of our church until gang violence took his life. For some reason, his death shook me. I think it was because I knew that no politician was going to come and make his death mean something or prevent future tragedies like Carlton's. The only help was going to come from God, me and the people. I buried Carlton. I gave his eulogy. Then I felt a nudge on my shoulder, and I turned around, but there was no one there. I felt the nudge again, and I knew it was from God. I walked out the door and across the street to the Super Motel, which was a hellhole of murder, drugs and prostitution. I said to myself, "Carlton’s death must mean something. It must move us to action." I placed a ladder against the side of the motel and climbed to the roof in the middle of the winter, where I stayed for 94 days. We raised enough to purchase the motel and tear it down. Instantly, the neighborhood saw a drop in overall crime. I knew it was Carlton saving lives. COREY BROOKS: CHICAGO SCHOOLS ARE FAILING KIDS AT THE ONE SKILL THAT CAN CHANGE THEIR LIVES It wasn’t the political class that did this. They would have talked themselves to death and planned themselves to death. It was the nudge from above that did this. It was the people who supported us through the entire journey that did this. It was that spark that set me off on a 15-year journey to build a community center in place of that motel. I even went back on top of a roof built atop shipping containers for 345 days to raise millions. All because I wouldn’t let Carlton’s death go to waste. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION Today, the Robert R. McCormick Leadership & Economic Opportunity Center stands impressively along King Drive. It is roughly 90,000 square feet of classrooms, trade training facilities, a gym, and a culinary school with restaurants opening onto the sidewalk. Within this space, people used to murder, fornicate and get high, and now, in this very same space, people are learning to wire a building, fix an engine and run a kitchen. If that is not a miracle, I don’t know what it is. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP I did all of this without government money. That is why I tell people to, yes, pay attention to elections and vote wisely. But I tell them to never put their fate in the hands of politicians. They work for us. Make them work for you. And throughout all of this, never lose sight of the most important American in your life: you. CLICK HERE TO READ MORE FROM PASTOR COREY BROOKS

articles.title: ASRA NOMANI: Far-left US groups battle Trump plan to rival China's tech dominance
articles.summary: The "Shut Down Pax" campaign, backed by CodePink and groups tied to Neville Roy Singham, fights President Donald Trump's bid to cut U.S. reliance on China.
articles.body: As President Donald Trump attends the 49th ASEAN Summit in the Philippines, American communist and far-left organizations are mobilizing internationally against an American initiative designed to reduce reliance on China. According to a Fox News Digital investigation, a network of 120 mostly communist, socialist and far-left U.S. groups – many of them pro-China – are joining protests in Asia opposing the Trump administration's effort to build an artificial intelligence and semiconductor hub in the Philippines that would reduce U.S. dependence on China in the AI war. The target is the Pax Silica tech industrial hub in the Philippines, which Undersecretary of State for Economic Affairs Jacob Helberg, a former senior adviser at Palantir Technologies, said last year would strengthen American control over AI infrastructure, semiconductor production and critical mineral supply chains. Two days ago, Helberg described Pax Silica as key to the world's "superintelligence revolution." The dispute centers partly on the proposed Clark Advanced Manufacturing Park, a roughly 4,000-acre development in New Clark City, Tarlac, in the Philippines, that would be a hub for the Pax Silica project. UPDATED – CHAOS INC.: COMMUNISTS, ANTIFA, AGITATORS IN THE RED-GREEN ALLIANCE A Fox News Digital investigation traced support for the protests to a transnational pro-China activist network stretching from Manila to New York, Washington, D.C., Los Angeles and Canada, including the Democratic Socialists of America East Bay, Calif., chapter and organizations with ties to American-born, Shanghai-based Marxist tech millionaire Neville Roy Singham. The protests also include indigenous groups in the Philippines that allege Pax Silica is being built on ancestral land. About eight of 10 of the organizations in the network of 120 are openly communist, socialist or "anti-imperialist." TRUMP TO SIGN TRADE DEAL AS HE KICKS OFF ASIA TRIP AHEAD OF NUCLEAR TALKS WITH XI AND PUTIN In addition, most of them are openly "anti-Zionist," opposed to the existence of a Jewish state of Israel, according to a Fox News Digital analysis of the groups in the network. CodePink, a pro-communist, pro-China nonprofit co-founded by Singham's wife, Jodie Evans, has used its media programming to criticize Pax Silica as a "military-industrial-surveillance complex." For Washington, experts say, the Pax Silica plan is about securing the technology and resources needed to compete with Beijing. For opponents, the protests are a way to curb American economic and military domination. The campaign also reveals how opposition to Trump's China strategy is being organized not only overseas, but through pro-China activist networks inside the United States. TRUMP LEAVES DOOR OPEN TO KIM JONG UN JOINING HIGH-STAKES TALKS WITH XI, PUTIN The U.S. network, organizing behind a campaign called "Shut Down Pax," includes familiar faces in the Singham network's protest circuit: BAYAN USA, a pro-communist Filipino American alliance helping lead the campaign; Anakbayan USA, a pro-communist youth organization; and the International League of Peoples' Struggle, or ILPS, founded with the help of Jose Maria Sison, the late founder of the Communist Party of the Philippines. The campaign has also reached the U.S. Congress. A letter, headlined "Shut Down Pax Silica in the Philippines" calls on lawmakers to halt the initiative pending review of environmental protections, labor rights and the treatment of Philippine communities. The activism intersects with other nonprofits in the network funded by Singham, including the People's Forum and BreakThrough News, that have promoted opposition to American foreign policy and challenged Washington's confrontation with Beijing. On Sept. 20, the U.S. chapter of the International League of Peoples' Struggle, the International Coalition for Human Rights in the Philippines-US and Bagong Alyansang Makabayan USA, or BAYAN USA, launched the "Shut Down Pax Silica Campaign Network" in Queens, New York, with organizers claiming about 500 participants in person and online. An article, published by Bulatlat, invoked a term popular in communist, "anti-imperialist" circles, claiming that a movement had begun in "the belly of the beast," with "resistance" to Pax Silica "rising." "We unite to confront and oppose the Trump/U.S.-led Pax Silica Initiative in its competition with China to dominate the AI/tech supply chain," the coalition declared in its organizing platform. FIRST ON FOX: ‘NO KINGS’ PROTEST NETWORK BEHIND FIGHT AGAINST AI DATA CENTERS AND FLOCK CAMERAS "We Filipinos in the U.S. must also take action," BAYAN USA declares on its campaign website, urging opposition to U.S. investments associated with Pax Silica. A month later, on Oct. 24, CodePink Radio published Episode 374, with host Marcy Winograd interviewing sociologist William Robinson about his new book, "Pax Silica: The New Ruling Class," examining the "rise of a new transnational capital complex" that combines big tech with global finance and the "military-industrial-surveillance complex" to "colonize the world unless we continue to protest, disrupt, divest and withhold our labor." The Black Alliance for Peace, which participated in CodePink's November "Taxpayer Uprising" campaign in Washington, D.C., last week, also promoted the anti-Pax Silica campaign's launch. Anakbayan USA, its local chapters and GABRIELA USA, a Filipino women's organization, appear among the American coalition's participants. Their Philippine counterparts are involved in the demonstrations surrounding Trump's visit. The coalition's published platform also identifies "Migrante USA," student organizations and other activist groups. The overlapping campaigns bring together Filipino American organizations, socialist activists and groups that have previously organized against U.S. military operations, Israel and American foreign policy. Singham, an American-born technology entrepreneur who sold his consultancy ThoughtWorks for an estimated $785 million in 2017, has financed an extensive network of U.S. nonprofits. A Fox News Digital investigation traced $278 million into six core American nonprofits, including CodePink, People's Forum, Tricontinental and BreakThrough BT Media Inc., which operates BreakThrough News. AMERICA RUNS ON DATA. IF WE DON’T BUILD THE INFRASTRUCTURE, CHINA WILL In July, the House Ways and Means Committee subpoenaed three organizations as lawmakers investigated the financial network and potential foreign influence. The organizations have challenged the investigation. One connection to the anti-Pax Silica campaign from the Singham network is "Nodutdol for Korean Community Development," an American group listed among the coalition's endorsers. Nodutdol member Winter Oh participated in the September launch in Queens. BreakThrough News has amplified the Philippine protests and criticism of Pax Silica, this summer promoting a BAYAN and Kilusang Mayo Uno demonstration with the slogan "The Philippines is not for sale!" As Trump was still in flight to Manila, BreakThrough news highlighted growing opposition to Pax Silica with a story headline, "ASEAN summit in Manila met with protests over Trump’s participation." Philippine officials have previously accused organizations such as Gabriela, Anakbayan, Karapatan and Kilusang Mayo Uno of acting as communist fronts. The groups have denied those allegations. CODEPINK LAUNCHES CHINA TOUR AS GRAND JURY INVESTIGATION INTO SINGHAM NETWORK FUNDING CONTINUES The ideological roots of the campaign extend to the Communist Party of the Philippines, founded by Sison in 1968. The United States designated the Communist Party of the Philippines and its armed wing, the New People's Army, as a foreign terrorist organization. In a Nov. 7 editorial, the party's official newspaper, Ang Bayan, urged Filipinos to organize "widespread protests" against Trump and to "reject and drive him out." The editorial accused Trump of advancing Pax Silica to strengthen American control over Philippine resources. The publication also reported that clandestine organizations associated with the National Democratic Front of the Philippines staged demonstrations. One teachers' group, KAGUMA, reportedly chanted, "Join the New People's Army!" The American campaign includes explicitly communist organizations, including the Workers World Party, a Marxist-Leninist organization, and the International Action Center. Separately, "Fight Back! News," published by the Freedom Road Socialist Organization, a Marxist-Leninist group that has organized many anti-ICE protests this year, republished an editorial from Ang Bayan criticizing Trump's Pax Silica initiative. CHINA ‘THROWING GASOLINE ON THE FIRE’ IN AI DATA CENTERS RACE, SAY LAWMAKERS The International League of Peoples' Struggle called for global protests under the slogans "Trump Out!" and "Reject Pax Silica!" The organization said groups planned demonstrations in 23 cities worldwide, including locations in the United States, Canada, Europe and Asia. American organizers identified planned actions in Los Angeles, Oregon, Washington, D.C., New York and Honolulu. In Ottawa, International League of Peoples' Struggle Canada, Anakbayan Ottawa, Migrante Ottawa and "Ottawa for Palestine" announced a demonstration for Wednesday outside the U.S. Embassy under the slogan "Shut the Pax Down!" In an April proposal to the U.S. State Department, Philippine officials outlined plans involving critical minerals, industrial infrastructure, investment and technology development. Protesters allege the project could displace Ayta Indigenous communities, expand mining, and strain electricity and water supplies. Philippine officials dispute allegations that the project would create a U.S.-controlled enclave or include the massive AI data centers described by activists. They say the development remains subject to Philippine law. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP As Trump arrived, demonstrations escalated. Reuters footage showed students marching with anti-Trump banners. SunStar reported more than 200 arrests during demonstrations in Metro Manila, while GMA News reported that activists condemned police dispersals and disputed the government's response.

articles.title: NSA's highly classified communications network disrupted by widespread outage
articles.summary: The National Security Agency's classified NSA Net faces an intermittent outage, with staggered arrivals preventing tens of thousands of logins at once.
articles.body: The National Security Agency's internal classified communications network is experiencing an "intermittent outage," but critical communications remain intact, a person familiar with the matter told Fox News Digital on Tuesday. The disruption affects a highly classified network known as NSA Net, which agency personnel use to communicate classified information internally. The latest impact at one of the nation's most sensitive intelligence agencies also comes amid a string of technology outages affecting major U.S. institutions, from the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to Microsoft and major banks, raising fresh concerns about the reliability of critical communications infrastructure. DHS CHIEF TELLS AMERICANS TO 'BREATHE' AMID TECH OUTAGES, INSISTS HOMELAND IS 'SECURE' CNN first reported the outage Tuesday, citing five people familiar with the matter. The agency has implemented staggered arrival times for personnel at NSA to prevent tens of thousands of employees from attempting to log into their computers simultaneously as officials work to address the disruption, the person familiar with the matter said. The issue appears to be technical in nature, according to the source, though the precise cause has not been established. Despite the disruption, the agency has not lost critical communications capabilities and has numerous backup facilities available to maintain operations, the source said. DUFFY: INVESTIGATORS EXAMINING 2 ROUTERS AFTER NATIONWIDE FAA GROUND STOP, NO SIGNS OF FOREIGN CYBERATTACK The NSA, which is responsible for collecting and analyzing foreign signals intelligence, plays a central role in supporting U.S. intelligence and military operations. It remains unclear when the outage began or how long it will take to fully restore the affected network. Fox News Digital reached out to the NSA for comment. The disruption comes amid a string of high-profile technology outages over the last week affecting government systems and major businesses. On Friday, the FAA ordered a nationwide ground stop after a telecommunications failure disrupted aircraft communications and radar feeds. The agency said instability spread to 17 of its 22 air route traffic control centers before flights resumed later that evening. The disruption was attributed by the FAA to excessive data flooding its aging telecommunications network, potentially originating from two facilities in Texas and Arkansas. Officials said they had found no indication of a cyberattack. Federal authorities are separately warning of increasingly sophisticated cyber threats. In a Nov. 13 advisory, the FBI warned that hackers are exploiting an artificial intelligence-powered penetration testing framework known as ARTEX to automate attacks against organizations worldwide. The FBI said the technology has allowed some attackers to move from initial targeting to privileged access in less than three hours. Microsoft previously linked the framework to a China-aligned hacking group's exploitation of a ConnectWise supply-chain compromise, which involved attempts to access more than 2,250 downstream Microsoft 365 customer environments. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP There is no evidence linking the NSA disruption to the ARTEX activity or the other recent outages.

articles.title: Obama-appointed judge paves way to unseal Ilhan Omar search warrant in blow to Trump's DOJ
articles.summary: A federal judge in Washington, D.C., paved the way to unseal the criminal search warrant and related documents against Rep. Ilhan Omar.
articles.body: A federal judge in Washington, D.C. who has often ruled against the Trump administration dealt a blow to the Justice Department Tuesday, paving the way to unseal the criminal search warrant and related documents against Rep. Ilhan Omar. Judge James Boasberg, who was appointed to the bench by former President Barack Obama in 2011, asked the DOJ's attorneys to submit proposed redactions to the documents to the court by Friday, and said he plans to unseal some materials Monday. Any parts of the warrant or related materials that are not submitted with redactions on Friday will be released, he said. While criminal warrants aren't typically unsealed until after charges are filed, 15 media organizations and watchdog group Judicial Watch sued to obtain the warrant. They have argued that releasing the contents of the warrant is in the public interest. 'RADICAL LEFT LUNATIC' JUDGE TRUMP WANTED IMPEACHED TAKES UP ILHAN OMAR WARRANT FIGHT The plaintiffs argued specifically that it should be made public which statutes federal investigators think Omar may have broken. Boasberg signaled that he would not release the warrant application, which is a sworn statement submitted to a judge explaining facts and evidence that establish probable cause for issuing a warrant. The DOJ did not immediately return Fox News Digital's request for comment. Omar is facing a probe related to whether she or her father fraudulently filled out immigration paperwork in order for her to obtain citizenship. The Somali-born congresswoman said last week that she wasn't privy to what exactly the DOJ is investigating. During the raid, which was conducted by Homeland Security Investigations (HIS), Omar's personal cellphone, computer and passport were seized. Her DNA has also been obtained, and her sister, Sahra Noor, was questioned by investigators the week of the raid. FEDERAL AGENTS SEIZE PHONE OF REP ILHAN OMAR IN RAID TIED TO IMMIGRATION FRAUD PROBE In a motion seeking to prevent the federal search warrant for the congresswoman’s home from being unsealed, the U.S. Attorney's Office for the District of Columbia referred to Omar as "Ilhan Nur Said Elmi, a/k/a Ilhan Abdullahi Omar…" and sources later told Fox News Digital that Ilhan Omar is not the congresswoman's "real name." That news caused speculation that Omar married her brother, Ahmed Nur Said Elmi, to resurface. The pair married in 2009, and officially divorced in 2017. ILHAN OMAR APPEARS CLUELESS ON BASIS FOR FEDERAL PROBES: ‘YOU PROBABLY HAVE MORE DETAILS ON THAT’ Omar has not been charged with a crime and has repeatedly and categorically denied any wrongdoing. She has characterized the investigation as politically motivated, saying President Donald Trump is targeting her. But the DOJ under former President Barack Obama opened an investigation into Omar's marriage with Nur Said Elmi in 2016 — suggesting the nonpartisan nature of some of the inquiries into the Minnesota lawmaker. OBAMA BACKS ILHAN OMAR AMID PROBE, ACCUSES TRUMP ADMIN OF 'APPALLING' TARGETING IN LENGTHY STATEMENT The New York Times first reported that Obama's FBI and Department of Homeland Security (DHS) began the probe in the summer of 2016, and that officials "found some evidence that [the marriage] was fraudulent." The Times reported that the investigation concluded when officials decided the potential felony crime was past the statute of limitations. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP That probe, an official told Fox News Digital, remained open until 2021, when it was closed under the Biden administration.

articles.title: SP’s initial offer: 24 seats; Cong will have to bargain hard for rest
articles.summary: SP may initially offer Congress about 24 UP seats based on 2022 vote performance, after Rahul Gandhi backs Akhilesh Yadav’s winnability criterion.
articles.body: Lucknow: With Rahul Gandhi endorsing Akhilesh Yadav’s “winnability” criterion for seat-sharing talks between the two INDIA bloc allies, the Samajwadi Party is likely to make an initial offer of around 24 seats where Congress candidates polled more than 20,000 votes in the 2022 UP elections. Congress may have to negotiate hard for additional seats it wants to contest.Political experts say during seat-sharing talks, parties are known to keep enough ‘leg room’ for negotiation manoeuvres in later stages of the talks.The decks were cleared for talks between the two parties during a conversation between Rahul and Akhilesh at Sonia Gandhi’s book launch in Delhi on Monday. Rahul was also told that SP was yet to constitute the team that will represent the party at the negotiations. The two sides later agreed to officially authorise party functionaries for formal seat-sharing talks likely to be held soon.UPCC working president Imran Masood has confirmed that his party’s top brass has had a word with the SP chief on the issue. “The SP chief has shared a ‘draft’ with our top leadership. articles.title: Van Hollen’s bid to replace Schumer as leader is putting pressure on Democrats to take sides
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — Senate Democrats elect their leader every two years behind closed doors and on a secret ballot. But this year’s race has burst into the pub...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — Senate Democrats elect their leader every two years behind closed doors and on a secret ballot. But this year's race has burst into the public eye as Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen mounts an insurgent bid against New York incumbent Chuck Schumer.

The Dec. 1 contest has put Senate Democrats on edge and has forced what could become an ugly fight immediately after major victories in the midterm elections . It has also put the more moderate incoming Democrats in a tough spot, forced to take sides in a leadership race before they are even sworn into office.

Schumer, who recruited several of those moderate Democrats who helped win the majority, has said he has the votes to be reelected , and around 15 of the 55 elected Democrats in next year's caucus have said publicly that they will support him. Four Democratic senators have said they will support Van Hollen. Everyone else is staying quiet for now.

"Leave it to the Democrats," said Colorado Sen. John Hickenlooper, who flipped an imaginary coin when asked by reporters on Monday how he would vote. "We flipped nine seats, and the person who actually helps put it all together and do all that, and all of a sudden, there's a revolt."

Van Hollen, who is backed by progressive groups, says it's time for new leadership after Schumer's nearly decade-long tenure. While the two men align on most issues, Van Hollen says Democrats need to more aggressively push to end the Iran war and potentially even shut down the government next month, if necessary, to stop the flow of war funding.

"To deliver, we need new leadership," Van Hollen says. "This isn't about any one person – it's about answering that call."

Van Hollen is making his argument to the public as Schumer mostly keeps quiet and holds private his conversations with the senators who will decide his fate. Schumer shared his agenda for the next Congress in a caucus luncheon last week, laying out a plan to try to quickly pass legislation on healthcare and tariffs and to launch multiple investigations into President Donald Trump's Republican administration.

Asked about Van Hollen's challenge on Tuesday, Schumer said again that he's confident he has the votes.

"We are united together on lowering costs and ending corruption," Schumer said.

The unusually public race — the first contested election for Senate Democratic leader in decades — comes when Schumer has drawn intense criticism from the party's base. Some voters and progressive groups called for his removal in 2025 after he voted with Republicans to keep the government open and as they called for stronger opposition to Israel's war in Gaza .

Still, many in the caucus see the role not as a national figurehead but as an inside operator who can navigate intraparty politics and the 100-member Senate's arcane rules to pass legislation.

"I want to hear from any candidate what their vision is for the floor and managing the caucus," said Georgia Sen. Jon Ossoff, who was just reelected. He said he hasn't committed to either Schumer or Van Hollen.

Party leaders also spend much of their time fundraising and recruiting candidates — a particular interest for Schumer, who has been directly or indirectly in charge of the Senate Democrats' campaign arm for two decades.

Most Democrats don't want to reveal their vote

Returning to Washington on Monday for the first time since Van Hollen entered the race, most Democrats would not answer questions about who they would support. That included prominent progressives like Massachusetts Sen. Elizabeth Warren.

Michigan Sen. Elissa Slotkin appeared last week at a press conference with Vermont Sen. Bernie Sanders , an independent who caucuses with Democrats, as he declared that he would not support Schumer. Van Hollen entered the race two days later, and Sanders immediately endorsed him. But Slotkin has not.

"I'm not saying anything," she told reporters on Monday.

Others like Virginia Sen. Tim Kaine defended Schumer while saying that they are still open to Van Hollen or someone else.

"Chuck delivered an amazing win," said Kaine. "Chuck knows Trump, and that will be really, really important going forward."

Still, Kaine said, "The voters are demanding change, so we have to figure that out as a caucus, and we're going to be able to. We're not afraid to have a discussion."

The eight incoming freshmen Democratic senators — nine if Mary Peltola wins the Alaska Senate race , which has still not been called — are set to alter the caucus next year. But only two have said how they will vote in the leadership election.

Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan and Peggy Flanagan of Minnesota, both of whom were backed by progressive groups in their campaigns, say they support Van Hollen. Schumer supported both of their opponents in their primaries, though he eventually put $67 million into El-Sayed's competitive race.

El-Sayed said Tuesday that he likes Schumer and will work alongside him if he wins. But he said he thinks Van Hollen is the best person to take on affordability challenges and liberal priorities like Medicare for All .

"We have not seen an open Senate fight for leadership for a very long time," El-Sayed said at The Atlantic Summit in Washington. "This is healthy. It's good."

For some of the other freshmen, many of them moderates from Republican-leaning states, the decision could be more difficult. Some said during their campaigns that they wouldn't vote for Schumer. But it's unclear if any of them would back the more liberal Van Hollen.

In South Carolina on Tuesday, Sen.-elect Annie Andrews , a doctor, said that she is in conversations with both candidates and has been "sharing my plans to fix our healthcare system."

Incoming Iowa Sen. Josh Turek told reporters he's met with both Schumer and Van Hollen. He said he wants more specifics on how they will help rural families, overhaul campaign finance and ban lawmakers from trading stocks. Turek said he also wants to assess "who is going to put forth the most robust anti-corruption agenda."

Hawaii Sen. Mazie Hirono, who is backing Schumer, said that the caucus needs to hear more from the new senators who "have been through the fire to get here."

"I think that we have to make sure that all these voices are heard," she said. "They've got a lot of talent to bring to the table."

Associated Press writers Joey Cappelletti and Kevin Freking in Washington, Meg Kinnard in Columbia, S.C., and Hannah Fingerhut in Des Moines, Iowa, contributed to this report.
